plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) to zero.
Reduce AI/Software leverage (METU, PLTU) to zero.
Trim QQQI concentration to 20% to reduce risk.
Add to SPY to increase broad index exposure.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation.
Expect lower volatility and modest returns.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for capital preservation with a target of around 1.5% monthly return. It significantly reduces leverage and concentration risk, holding a larger cash buffer. Drawdowns should be minimal, but upside potential is also capped.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) to minimal levels.
Reduce AI/Software leverage (METU, PLTU) to manage risk.
Trim QQQI concentration to 20%.
Buy XLV for defensive sector exposure.
This plan balances growth with risk management.
Expect moderate returns with controlled drawdowns.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets around 2.5% monthly return by managing risk first. It trims leverage and concentration while adding a defensive sector. A moderate cash buffer is maintained. Upside is balanced against the potential for drawdowns.

plan: Increase leveraged ETF exposure (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) to 6% each.
Increase AI/Software leverage (METU, PLTU) to 6% each.
Trim QQQI concentration to 15%.
Buy XLV for defensive sector exposure.
This plan aggressively pursues growth through leverage and concentration.
Expect higher potential returns but also significantly larger drawdowns.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% monthly return by leaning into leverage and concentration, including leveraged ETFs. It maintains a smaller cash buffer. While upside potential is maximized, this strategy carries the highest risk of substantial drawdowns due to leverage and potential ETF decay. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Sell all high-beta, leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, PLTU) to zero.
Increase QQQI allocation to 30% for income generation.
Add to SPY for broad market exposure and stability.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly income.
Expect low volatility and reliable distributions.
NAV can still decline in market selloffs.
income.read: This income-focused plan targets around 1% monthly return through distributions. It eliminates leveraged and high-beta assets, concentrating on income-generating ETFs like QQQI and broad index ETFs like SPY. While aiming for low drawdowns and consistent income, the Net Asset Value (NAV) can still decrease during market downturns.
